name: Liao dynasty (Khitan, Shengzong)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 2.0-2.5 million km2 for 1000-1100 (mid 2.25M). The infobox of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty gives 2.6 million km2 (947 est., Taagepera 1997 and Turchin et al. 2006; high). The world_1000 Liao polygon measures only 0.79 million km2 (low): it leaves out the Mongolian steppe the Liao controlled.

population.note: Seshat codes 3.8 million for the Liao (907-1125). The Liao dynasty article gives a peak of "750,000 Khitans and two to three million ethnic Han Chinese" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty), 2.75-3.75 million (low). High adds about 20% for Bohai, Xi and tribal peoples outside both counts, a judgement.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Five capitals and the walled prefectural towns of the Han south; the Khitan majority of the north lived in camps.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. One ordo of 15,000 households could field up to 6,000 horsemen; Empress Dowager Xiao's own ordo 10,000 cavalry; by the end of the dynasty (1125) all the imperial ordos together held 81,000 Khitan and 124,000 Bohai and Chinese households able to field 101,000 horsemen (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty). In 1004 fewer ordos existed than in 1125, so the ordo cavalry is guessed at 40,000-70,000, plus tribal frontier armies and Han garrisons of the Southern Capital circuit. Chronicle figures (300,000 troops in 947, Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288; 400,000 for the 1010 Goryeo campaign, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty) are not used as counts.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Tribal levies and Han Chinese militia; the high end is the 400,000 claimed for the 1010 Goryeo campaign.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Han siege engineers, herd guards for remounts, courier and staff personnel.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Every Khitan tribesman served as a mounted warrior, while the Han and Bohai farmers were drafted only as militia; below the 0.2 of a pure steppe confederation (xiongnu--200).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured Khitan cavalry, organised in groups of 500 to 700 men (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: armoured riders on armoured horses

training.note: Rubric 0.75: ordo guards bound to the emperor

count.note: Educated guess. Horse archers of the ordos and the tribes, each man with remounts.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: composite bows, several horses per man

count.note: Educated guess. Han Chinese and Bohai infantry garrisons in the south.
Educated guess. Traction trebuchets with Han engineers for siege work on the Song frontier.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: the 1004 campaign under Shengzong and the Empress Dowager reached the Yellow River about 160 km from the Song capital and forced the Treaty of Chanyuan (Song recognition as peers and 200,000 bolts of silk and 100,000 taels of silver a year), though the main general Xiao Talin was killed by a Song crossbow (Wright 2008 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanyuan_Treaty)

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: each emperor's ordo guard was his own household ("heart and belly guard", Atwood 2004 via Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288); Han and Bohai units less bound

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: an offensive war against the Song a decade after the 992 invasion of Goryeo (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty); a dynasty near its height

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: composite bows, lances, crossbows, traction trebuchets.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4 (barding at 4): armoured heavy cavalry and horses.

ships.note: Anchor 1-2: river craft only; no navy.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: walled capitals and prefectural towns built on Chinese models.

logistics.note: Anchor 3: self-supplied cavalry with remounts and foraging; "smashing the pasture and grain" in 947 (Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (via OWID, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): China 1000 = 1,225 (2011 int$), the high. The Liao economy was pastoral in the north and frontier farming in the south, placed below the Song level.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A militarised dual state; much of the cost fell on tribesmen who armed and horsed themselves.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron working, salt, textiles and ceramics in the Han south.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Millet and wheat farming in the south and Liaodong, pastoral herds in the north.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads linking the five capitals and the passes of the Yan mountains.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Bohai Gulf coast; no seagoing fleet recorded.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Coastal and river craft; trade with the Song went overland through border markets.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry with remounts living off pasture and plunder; less than a pure steppe army because the Han infantry and siege train move slowly.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, oxen, camels; the 1082-83 snowfall killed 60-70% of tribal livestock and a horse shortage was noted in 1043 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: the Yan mountain passes and walled Southern Capital, steppe depth and a harsh continental winter.

notes: Snapshot = autumn 1004, the Chanyuan campaign under Shengzong and the Empress Dowager Xiao Yanyan, ended by the Treaty of Chanyuan in January 1005. Population and area are Seshat codings. The army is the weakest set of values: the only structured figures (ordo households and horsemen) describe the dynasty at its end in 1125, and chronicle totals of 300,000-400,000 are not used. Border: world_1000 Liao is the file at or before the year; the polygon covers Manchuria, the Liao River and the Sixteen Prefectures but not the Mongolian steppe, so areaKm2 is researched. Population convention: everything the dynasty ruled, Khitan and Han.
